Le fratture dell'avambraccio distale del: Fractures of the distal forearm in children should be described by location (metaphysis, physis, diaphysis), completeness (torus, greenstick, complete), displacement and angulation on the lateral view, and for the other bone. Here the line crosses the whole radial metaphysis and the distal fragment is angulated dorsally; the ulna, according to the collection's annotation, has an incomplete metaphyseal fracture, hardly evident here: when the radius is broken, the second bone should always be carefully searched and, if doubtful, reported as such. Complete and angulated fractures are not as stable as torus fractures: they require reduction (if the angulation exceeds what remodeling can correct for the age) and a cast with follow-up. Distinguish Galeazzi (radius + distal radioulnar dislocation) and Monteggia (ulna + radial head dislocation).
